items.title: Story mission

sections.title: GRAPHICS PRESETS
lines: The Graphics Preset row (Options > Graphics Settings in the pause menu, Options > Graphics in the main menu) has six presets: Classic (the vanilla look and limits: original draw distance, painted sky, 14 cars and 15 pedestrians, no extra effects, runs only at the original 30 / 25 frames per second), Classic: Extended (the same look with a larger draw distance, more traffic and pedestrians, dynamic shadows and any frame rate), Extended: Low / Medium / High / Max (procedural sky, grass, reflections, render scale, view distance and the far traffic layer step by step; Max is the default). You can go back to Classic at any time without a restart; changing a single option afterwards shows Custom. Console: preset [0-5 or name]. Texts in 12 languages are machine translated.

What a preset sets: the draw distance (10 / 48 / 120 / 200 / 300 / 400 map cells from Classic to Max), the sky (the original painted sky in the two Classic presets, the procedural sky from Low up), the sun shadows (off in Classic, on in every other preset, also with the painted sky), 3D grass (Medium and up), reflections of cars, wet roads and windows (Medium and up) and of water (High and up), the lights on cars and lamps (Medium and up), the number of traffic cars and pedestrians, the far traffic and crowd layer, cars of other cities (Low and up), the render scale (80 % in Low, 90 % in Medium, 100 % otherwise), smooth drawing between logic ticks and the frame rate limit. Classic locks the frame rate to the game clock (30, or 25 with PAL Speed); leaving Classic gives back the FPS limit you had before. NOT part of any preset: texture filtering, PGXP, VSync, window mode, resolution, the HUD, the day cycle, horizon fog, the texture manager, the number of players and PAL Speed.

Switching a preset inside a level works at once, but it also changes the draw distance and the traffic and pedestrian numbers from that moment on, which are part of the simulation: replays and online games compare these settings and refuse to mix them. A fresh install starts in Extended: Max, which is what the defaults were before the presets existed, so the picture does not change. Presets 1 to 5 were not compared with a real Max install by a person.

Procedural Sky (Options > Graphics Settings) is its own row and switches between the procedural sky and the original painted sky at any time, also in a level; the presets only set it. config.ini [render] proceduralSky is the starting value.

Preset frame cap fixes: a limit of exactly 25 or 30 is read as the Classic lock and is never remembered as your own limit when you leave Classic; a broken fpsfree= value in config\display.ini (negative, 1 to 19 or above 1000) means unlimited instead of capping the game at a few frames per second.

The rain streaks are drawn by the graphics card now and the row "rain" (console: tweak rain) is their amount in percent of the 4000 streak pool, 0 meaning none. Classic and Classic: Extended set 15 (about the number of drops the original rain had on screen), Extended: Low 20, Medium 25, High and Max 50 (config.ini rainDensity, default 50). The streaks are thinner and straighter than the original trails.
config.ini wholeMap is gone: the whole map is always on (the old world drawing was removed, wholeMap=0 drew no world at all). A leftover key is ignored and written to the log.

sections.title: GRAPHICS (the renderer)
lines: The 3D world is drawn by the graphics card only: buildings, roads, ground, the far city, grass, the sky, cars, the far traffic and crowd layer (its lamps and lit windows at night too), pedestrians (models and shadows), smoke, sparks, debris, leaves, birds, tyre tracks, light glows, lens flares, explosions, target arrows, helicopter rotors and rain. The old way of drawing the world with the processor (the PlayStation style polygon painter) is deleted, with its switches: Options > Graphics > GPU Static Batch, Options > Graphics > GPU Cars, config.ini [game] gpuBatch, gpuCars and drawDistance. Menus, the front end, fades, movies, text and the classic HUD still use the old 2D drawing path. Translucent things are sorted per object now, not per polygon like the PlayStation did, so a few overlaps (smoke over glass, for example) can differ from the original.

Draw distance: the original game drew a diamond of 21 map cells and that is what the View Distance values 1, 8 and 10 mean now. For values from 21 to 169 the fog now ends exactly at the distance you set (it used to cut the world in steps of 32 cells behind a fog that ended at 170), so these settings look smoother and slightly different than before; the default 400 looks the same. Split screen fog is closer by design (see below).

Split screen is smooth: it used to be drawn 30 times a second whatever your PC could do; every view is drawn at your frame rate now, with the camera and the cars blended between two logic ticks (2 to 8 players, also in the pause menu, which freezes the world and draws every frame). Cuts of the camera are not blended. NOT drawn that way: fast forward, screen fades, mission titles, in-game cutscenes, replays and demos.

Effects move smoothly at any frame rate (smoke, sparks, debris, leaves, birds, rain, splashes, tyre tracks used to move 30 times a second) and the logic tick owns them: smoke of a car is made for every car near a view, not only for cars that were drawn; debris and leaves are only removed when they are out of range of every split screen view. The rain is a pattern of streaks that depends on the game clock, so two runs of the same rain scene look the same; Pause menu has no row for it, console:  tweak rain  (percent).
Pedestrians in split screen use the same fast drawing as in a one player game (they used the slow processor drawing before).

Speed, measured on one PC (1080p, RTX 5080, vsync off, other programs running, numbers move by +-10 % from run to run): one player in the rush hour scene with 116 cars about 560 - 700 frames per second; 4 players at the long view distance 115 -> 168 and 8 players 63 -> 88 after the split screen changes; 1000 frames per second for one player was NOT reached (one run on a quiet PC read 825). Render Scale (below) is the lever when the graphics card is the limit.

Present path: config\display.ini  present=1  (default) makes the game hand every drawing pass to the driver at once, which cut the wait at the end of a frame. present=0 restores the old order. The key is written by the options menu; there is no menu row for it.

Render Scale (Options > Display Settings, pause menu and front end; config\display.ini  renderscale=100): draws the 3D world at 50 - 100 % of the window size (100 / 90 / 80 / 75 / 70 / 60 / 50) and scales it up, while the HUD, minimap and console stay sharp. Only with ONE player: split screen, the front end and the map screen are not scaled.

Water Brightness (Options > Display Settings; config\display.ini  waterbrightness=100; console:  water [25-200]): 25 - 200 % in steps of 5, 100 = unchanged. It scales the sea you see below the horizon (Havana lake, Rio sea, the Chicago lake) and the water surfaces of the level. with the painted sky the lower half of the painted dome is not scaled.

Painted sky: the water reflection (water surfaces: the river and lake pieces of the core pack, edit pack water, the Driver 1 water plane) now shows the painted sky when you play with Procedural Sky off (it showed a made up sky colour before). Seen only in a debug picture of the reflection, not on screen in a normal run. The car environment reflection still has no sky with the painted sky.

Sun shadows with the painted sky: Sun Shadows work with the original sky too. The painted sun is only about 19 degrees above the horizon, which put the whole street in the shadow of one row of houses, so by day the shadows use the painted sun's direction lifted to at least 34 degrees; at dusk 9 degrees, at night the shadow comes from the painted moon.

Removed: the upscaled "HQ" sky pictures (240 files, about 190 MB). They never loaded in the game (a file name bug), so nothing changes in the picture; the setup no longer has the step "Sharper skies" and the game uses the procedural sky or the original sky. An old install keeps the unused files, delete GAME_DATA\DRIVER2\GFX\HQ\sky*.tga to get the space back (the fonts in that folder stay). Also removed: GPU Static Batch, GPU Cars, the unused car chrome map (see CARS AND TRAFFIC).

The pause menu and the front end Display Settings / Graphics Settings pages are the places for all of this: Display Settings has Render Scale and Water Brightness, Graphics Settings has Graphics Preset, View Distance, Sun Shadows, Procedural Sky, the reflections, 3D Grass.

sections.title: PLAYERS (split screen)
lines: Up to 8 local players. 2 players are stacked, 3 and 4 players share the window in quarters, 5 to 8 players get a grid of smaller views. Every player has his own view, minimap, HUD (speed, rev arc and gear, damage, wanted bar, fuel, clock), police chase, fuel tank, wallet, jobs, CB radio offers, fares and traffic stops. The text of the HUD stays readable down to 720p.

Main menu > Multiplayer has two pages, Local and Online. Local: 2 to 8 players, the game mode and a car picker where every player picks his car at the same time (ready flags, the game starts 15 seconds after the first one is ready, bots can fill seats). Pause menu > Game Modes > Players restarts with 1 to 8 players.

Profiles per player seat: every seat can use its own profile (or Guest). A profile keeps its own money, respect and start car; volume and high score table belong to the computer, not to the profile. Multiplayer menu has a profile row per player; Options > Controls > Local Players > Profile for player 1; a manage screen renames and deletes profiles (a deleted profile is moved to saves\_deleted, not erased).

Car picker: the Start button puts the car this profile used last under the cursor, every further press the car of the next player who is already ready ("Same as player N"), then it starts over; moving the cursor by hand starts the cycle again. 3 new texts, machine translated.

Game modes for 2 to 8 players: Checkpoint Race, Gate Race, Trail Blazer, Survival, Cops 'n' Robbers (2 rounds, the teams swap), Capture the Flag (2 teams, 3 captures) and Courier (below). Prize money and a results panel at the end. Pause menu > Game Modes.

Shared CB radio (2 to 8 players, free roam): one package offer for everybody instead of one per player. Join with the take-it key, the first joined car at the pickup loads it, a carrier whose car is badly damaged (or who gets out for 3 s) drops it where he stands and anybody in a car can drive into it and deliver it; every change of hands adds 25% to the pay (up to 75%). Nobody pays a fine. With two players or more the CB offers no private package runs. One player is unchanged.

Courier game mode (Game Modes menu and Multiplayer, 2 to 8 players, CB radio on): eight minutes of the shared package run back to back; the score is the dollars you delivered, the usual prize money comes on top.

Fuel, money, felony, jobs, fares and traffic stops are kept per player now. Job pay used to go to the wallet of player 1 whoever drove the job; it goes to the player who did it. The traffic stop fine and the time bonus of the mission maker are charged / paid to the right player too.
The second player (and the others) can get out of the car; players that a mission start leaves behind are placed beside player 1; the start car you chose now also applies to the driving game modes.

Controllers: the keyboard can be several players (4 key sets: arrows, WASD, IJKL, numpad), 8 gamepads work, and every key set / gamepad can be given to a player, or nobody, while playing (pause menu > Controllers; Options > Controls > Keyboard Plays As). Vibration works on every pad. Face Buttons (by label / by position) for Nintendo style pads in Pause > Controllers and Options > Controls.

Tyre tracks, smoke and hubcaps for players 3 to 8; a split screen on a very wide window no longer cuts off the world; split screen frames are no longer stretched like menu frames; a freeze when two players drove far apart (or one was wanted off the map) was fixed (please confirm).
Pause menu in a split screen game: a modern menu over the whole window with Game Modes and Options.

Split screen speed: every view draws its far city shorter (the fog comes closer in a quarter of the screen), with smaller shadow and reflection maps, and far traffic, shadow casters and the ambient cars are drawn in far fewer GL calls: 4 players at the long view distance went from about 115 to about 168 frames per second, 8 players from about 63 to about 88 (1080p, RTX 5080, vsync off); one player is unchanged except that the rush hour scene draws about 15 % faster.

Online is NOT a feature of this version. The early test code is still in the build (Multiplayer > Online: Host game / Join by address, a lobby with seats, car picker and ready flags); it was only run between two games on ONE PC over the loopback address, with simulated packet loss, and NEVER over a network or the internet. Development is on hold; do not rely on it.

sections.title: SOUND
lines: More sound channels: 32 voices instead of 24, music moved to the last 8 voices, 24 sound effect channels instead of 16. With more than 4 players every engine keeps its rev and idle loop (one shared horn). Players 3 and 4 get their tyre skid again. Engines and horns were listened to on 2026-10-23 (also after the sound decode cache below) and sounded fine. NOT listened to: the music on the upper voices, tyre skids, idle, and the engines of players 3 to 8.
Driver 1 crash sounds are louder (all three strengths come from the heavy crash sample of the disc). Run the setup again to remake them. NOT listened to since.
A far away source (a cop smashing at the edge of the map) is silent now instead of wrapping around to a near, very loud sound (distances are 64 bit).
The game is muted while the setup lets it build the city maps.

sections.title: LOOK
lines: Roads: the wide pale bands for lane markings and crossings (a low detail road drawn from the whole-map renderer) are gone: every object, roads included, is drawn with its most detailed model at every distance. The first start after the update rebuilds the map cache once. In Chicago the map batch grew by about 20 MB (125 to 145 MB) and the frame time did not change.
3D grass patches follow the slope of the ground.
Main menu: a new background (also a wide one for ultrawide screens) and music (an mp3 that fades out on its own while a game loads). The idle demo starts after 3 min 15 s.

Demos: recorded drives. Pause > Demos records one (up to 6 minutes), plays a random one or opens the demos folder; the main menu plays a random one when nobody touches it. A demo is one file (about 2 to 3 MB per minute) you can share; it plays without any simulation, so it looks the same on every install (details: MODDING_GUIDE.txt, section 8).
Minimap: Options > Display > Minimap Style Round or Square, and Minimap Size % for the square one; the classic HUD map fills its square box; the minimaps of a split screen follow the style.

Customize: choosing it on foot no longer freezes the game; every built-in lamp has a Visible row and a Make editable lamp row; adding and deleting a lamp or an exhaust rebuilds the rows (a crash from a bug report).

My Cars (Pause menu > Customize): the button My Cars (or the M key, or the pad Select button) opens the list of the cars you saved: Save current car (you name it, the default is the model name), put one on (the car AND its paint, wheel design and finish, rim size and engine sound come back), rename, copy, delete. Every profile has its own list; a Guest uses the list of the host (player 1's profile). The cars you customized before are taken over once from the old per-car look file. A saved car whose mod was removed stays in the list, greyed. 25 new texts, machine translated (native review needed).
The day to night swap keeps the textures of car pages that hold other pictures than the level's own (Vegas page 41 and others).

sections.title: CARS AND TRAFFIC
lines: Cars are always drawn by the graphics card: the option Options > Graphics > GPU Cars, config.ini [game] gpuCars and the old CPU car drawing (the polygon plotters, the CPU wheels and exhaust pipes, the low detail model switch) are gone. Models made of flat or textured triangles only (some Gran Turismo 2 and Driver 1 cars), the mini cars cheat wheels and a model with broken vertex numbers now draw like any other car; a model without any polygon is the only car left out (the log names its slot). pgxpTextureMapping=0 no longer changes how cars are drawn.

Removed: the unused chrome reflection map of the cars (it was off by default and had no option; the cars use the world reflection, Options > Graphics > Car Reflections). The developer variables REDRIVER_CHROME, REDRIVER_GTREFL and REDRIVER_OLDREFL are gone.
Traffic: the police cars of the other cities no longer drive around as civilian cars (they stay in the customizer list, now labelled Police).

Mods on borrowed cars: the car models, cosmetics (wheel places, lights) and denting files of a mod (BetterCars ...) now also apply to the cars of another city seen in the traffic. Their texture pages still do not, unless the texture manager is switched on (below).

Driver 1 cars (PlayStation): scaled to fit the Driver 2 traffic: the cruisers are no longer taller and longer than the Driver 2 police car (light bar scaled with the body), long cars are shortened a little, the collision box is as wide as the car. The 30 PC cars use the same fit. Run the setup again to remake the cars.
A rare use of an uninitialised value in the traffic AI (a car that lost its road) was fixed; the cars keep their road rules in whole numbers (the same traffic on every computer).

Random numbers: the traffic, pedestrian, police and event decisions now come from a real random generator with its own saved state (before, every call in a tick got a number worked out from the tick count, the ped clothes colours had only a few combinations and every level started with the same numbers). Every city and mission starts with its own numbers, a restart gives the same game as a fresh start. Replays recorded with an older version are refused with a message (they would play a different game): record them again (the replay file marker is RDF2; older files carry another marker).

sections.title: GAS STATIONS
lines: config\gasstations.txt has 13 more lines for Las Vegas and Rio from a player survey and 3 more Las Vegas stations found in the level data (rdinspect gasstations). Havana and the Driver 1 cities have no gas station objects in their level data.

sections.title: TEXTURES (for modders, off by default)
lines: Texture manager: textures as pictures without the 256 x 256 page or 16 colour limit. It is OFF by default; [game] texMgr=1 in config\config.ini switches it on (texMgrBudgetMB sets its memory). It covers the car pages (a car file cars\<name>.png replaces the pages of a car, the BetterCars style PAGE_n\*.TIM files now reach the borrowed cars too, and the customizer paints and the night swap follow) and, new, the texture pages of the whole level: roads, buildings and the far city are drawn from the manager's pictures with their palettes, and the day to night swap fades between the two sets as the page path does (the Driver 1 cities have no night set). The pictures are the same as the page path draws; a PNG for roads and buildings does not exist yet, they still come from the PAGE_n .TIM files of a mod. Level editor pieces stay on the old page path. Experimental: with it on the cars are drawn from the same pictures as before, and it costs a little graphics card time per frame. Palette rows of cars and levels that are no longer used are given back now, so a long session or a trip to other cities does not fill the table (a stress run did).

Level content package (a skeleton, off by default): rdcontent package import <day.LEV> --out <folder> --id <city key> [--night <night.LEV>] turns a level of your own disc into a folder (level.txt, sim, tex, materials.txt) and rdcontent package --verify <folder> [--against <day.LEV>] checks it. With [game] contentLoader=1 in config\config.ini the game reads the level data and the texture pixels of content\<city key> instead of the LEV when the package is complete and its checksums match, and falls back to the LEV with a log line otherwise. The result is the same game; the LEV is still needed for the streamed city parts. Nothing makes the package for you yet and nobody has played with the option on.

Texture dump for modders: rdinspect texdump writes every texture of a Driver 2 city as a PNG, rdinspect texpack turns edited PNGs back into the .TIM files the game loads (MODDING_GUIDE.txt, section 9: replacing road and world textures). The textures are not shipped, you dump them from your own disc.

sections.title: LEVEL EDITOR
lines: OBJ import: the sample OBJ files that ship in samples\Car Templates start with a comment line  # scale reference: ...  that the importer read as a scale of 0, so every point landed on one spot and the nine pieces were invisible. The header is only taken as a scale when a positive number follows it now; the pickup stands on the road at its real size.

Checkpoint lap text: the HUD showed a question mark instead of  LAP 0:00  or  CHECKPOINT 1  1 / 2  (the message pointed at memory that was already gone). Seen correct on the HUD at night after the fix. Two checkpoints that overlap repeat the lap message every frame by design: place gates apart.

Editor files that are damaged are read with limits now: a line longer than 4096 characters is skipped with its tail, numbers are clamped (coordinates inside +-10 000 000, texture and palette numbers 0 - 65535), every list has a size limit (a file past it stops loading with a log line), and one log line says how many damaged lines were skipped. A shared edit file can no longer crash the game while it loads.

Checked with the new renderer in an automatic run (empty edit folder, also with [game] texMgr=1): place, move, copy / paste, duplicate, delete, undo / redo, save, leave and re-enter, relaunch and load (153 pieces equal before and after), OBJ import and its undo. No crash and no broken picture.

"Dark texture on fence or canal pieces" (a report) could NOT be reproduced. Things that look dark by design: the green tint of a selected piece, a floor quad lying exactly in the road plane (move it UP), and a piece takes the light value of the texture you sampled it from. A piece with a cut-out texture (chain link) casts a solid shadow rectangle in the sun shadow map; this is the best guess for the report and is not fixed. Tell us the tab, button and time of day if you see it.
NOT verified: the warm pool of a LIGHT marker at night (the ring is drawn, the pool was not told apart from the street lamps in a picture).

sections.title: STABILITY (damaged or hostile files)
lines: A review of everything the game reads found places where a damaged file could crash or hang it; the fixes: damaged or cut-off replay files are refused; a damaged or cut-off music file logs  [music] song is ...  and is skipped (checked with made up songs only: NOT with a real MUSIC.BIN); sound banks, voices and the sound memory writes are range checked; mission files with wrong text offsets show no text instead of crashing; a wrong mission ladder position in a save is clamped; a language file is read once and switching language 100 times does not grow memory; the menu music fade cannot run into a closed audio device; a zip with a lie in its size field (zip bomb) is refused while installing a mod and parts that were unpacked are removed again; mod conflict scanning does not follow links; a job without pickup: or drop: is skipped with a log line instead of going to 0,0; a car file or a car package that is damaged is skipped with a log line  [d1car] ... is damaged: not loaded  /  [pkgcars] ...: not loaded .

Saving: every write is checked before the old file is touched; the old file is kept and a log line says so when the disk is full. (Loading does not fall back to the .bak copy on purpose: it could bring back progress you deleted.)

sections.title: LANGUAGES
lines: 117 new texts (CB package, Courier, Multiplayer Local / Online, car picker, profile screens) are translated into the 12 languages by machine; a native speaker has not read them yet. Translation status for translators: rdloc report.

sections.title: GAME ENGINE (what you notice)
lines: The game logic runs on a steady 30 Hz clock that catches up when a frame is late, the same for every number of players. Restarting a level now gives exactly the same game as a fresh start (traffic stops, jobs, CB radio, fares, police, day clock and the random numbers were not all reset before).

The game is built with SSE float maths and fixed compiler settings, so every build gives the same simulation (a step towards playing online together). Two bugs behind rare traffic differences between builds were fixed on the way (an unset value in the traffic lane code, and a rounding step in the traffic avoidance).
A watchdog writes a [freeze] line and the registers into logs\crash.txt when the game draws no frame for a long time, so a freeze can be reported.

The emulated PlayStation geometry engine (GTE: the register file and its instructions) is gone. The car, collision, camera and event maths is plain integer code that gives the same numbers, and the drawing passes its poses explicitly. You should notice nothing; the old 2D drawing path of the menus and the ordering tables still exist.
Prize money of a race is exact (a float sum made a prize one dollar short in some cases); the day clock, sun height, taxi meter, race distances and fuel use whole numbers now.

sections.title: TOOLS (no Python anywhere any more)
lines: Every tool of the project is a C program now; the Python tools are gone. Modder tools in tools\ (optional download): rdcontent (mission / pack / chase, car sheet / import / verify / pack / export / list, package, site), rdinspect (iso, psexe, levdump, texstat, texdump, texpack, carstats, carsheet, gtsheet, gasstations, d1carview and more), rdloc (translation status). The same programs at the source level: rdcheck (code health), rdtest (game tests, bench), rdassets, rdbuild.

rdcontent car sheet: checks the performance sheet (sheet.txt) of a custom car, prints its hash, writes a template (street, sport, muscle, truck). MODDING_cars_handbook.md is the specification (v0.1, provisional); the OBJ templates are in samples\Car Templates.

rdcontent car, the rest of the car commands: import obj <car.obj> --id <id> --class <class> --out <folder> (OBJ + PNG pictures -> a car package folder), verify [--drive] <package folder> (the checks, with --drive also 0-60 mph, 0-100 mph, 400 m and top speed from the sheet), pack, hash, stat, drive <sheet.txt> and export <package folder> <out.zip>.

Car packages in the game: a folder mods\<mod>\cars\<id>\ with car.txt, sheet.txt, cosmetics.txt, model\ (OBJ text, three detail levels) and tex\ (PNG) is checked, turned into a car the engine knows (cached in cache\pkgcars) and listed with the other cars (picker, customizer, traffic with kind street). OFF by default: create config\carpkg.ini with the line  enabled=1 . A damaged package is skipped with a log line  [pkgcars] ...: not loaded , the good ones of the same folder still load; five kinds of damage were tried in the game. To make the car drive from its sheet (engine curve, gearbox, tyres) also create config\carsheet.ini with  enabled=1  (and optionally  preset=real|scaled|capped , real is the default); without it the package car drives like a normal Driver 2 sedan.

The Car Creator window, reDriver_CarCreator.exe (tools\car_gui, built with rdbuild build cargui): pick an OBJ (and one wheel OBJ, which it mirrors to four) and a PNG, fill in the sheet in a form with 0-60 / top speed numbers shown live and a side / top / front preview with the Driver 2 sedan outline, read the messages with a fix hint for each, build the package, copy it into a mod and test it in the game. It is a thin layer over the same code as rdcontent car, so both give identical packages. It is in the modder tools download and next to the game exe.

Gran Turismo sheets: rdinspect gtsheet --gt1 <Gran Turismo disc> --out <folder> writes a sheet.txt for each of the 178 cars of the first game and rdinspect gtsheet --gt2 <Gran Turismo 2 Simulation Mode disc> --out <folder> for all 621 cars of the second (power, mass, gearbox, tyre grip, drive type; real figures of your own disc). Checked against 30 real cars by the numbers the author remembered (unverified, from memory): mean error power 3 %, top speed 4 %, 0-60 mph 8 %. In the game four GT2 sheet cars reach the reference 0-60 time within 2 %. A rear-heavy rear-drive car (NSX, Viper) no longer launches like a front-drive car when it drives from a sheet. Brakes of sheet cars are still the Driver 2 brakes; speeds above 167 mph could not be checked in a city.

rdcontent car list <game folder or mod folder>: prints the car catalog the game builds (id, source, kind, class, rarity, sheet hash, optional 0-60 and top speed of the sheet) without starting the game. In the game the car pool, the car pickers, the customizer and the traffic menu now read one catalog; a car that has a performance sheet shows its 0-60 mph, top speed and class in the customizer (Car tab) and in the multiplayer car picker.
rdinspect texdump / texpack: see TEXTURES and MODDING_GUIDE.txt section 9 (rdinspect texpack --selftest checks the converter without game data).

Project website: rdcontent site --out <folder> [--public | --internal] builds a static web page (overview, roadmap, changelog, known issues, how to report a bug with the logs that are needed) from the project's to-do list and this changelog. The public view shows only the items marked public and is scanned for private paths and names before anything is written. The page uses no scripts or fonts from other sites and no cookies; its only network request, once a project address is filled in, is reading the public GitHub issue list. Nothing is hosted yet and no project address is set.

Build and release tooling: no scripts any more. The only script is bootstrap.cmd, which compiles rdbuild.exe; rdbuild builds every tool and the game, makes the release package, the project website and the public snapshot; rdtest runs the tests (source tree only).
Release checks (for the package makers): the package is scanned for files that must not ship (game data, disc files, the dropped HQ sky) before it is built.
Setup: the game is muted while it builds the maps; the converters for Driver 1 and Gran Turismo cars, sounds and wheels are in C and give the same files as before.
Linux: the Python installer is gone; the way is Proton (Steam Play) with linux\README_LINUX.txt.

sections.title: Changes
lines: Level editor: the menu dropdown no longer clicks through to the buttons below it; a box select over original faces is instant (it cast 600 rays before) and the green highlight shows every selected face, tinted and outlined; a piece whose outline passes within a few pixels of the cursor is picked even when the ray misses it.
Level editor looks: every colour follows the HUD theme (70s, PlayStation, Driver Menu, mod themes; VIEW > Next theme), the piece list shows a thumbnail of each piece's texture.

Level editor keys: F1 opens the manual, the polygon keys are F2 / F3, HELP > Keyboard shortcuts lists every shortcut (one table, checked for clashes at start); the renderer's own debug keys (F3, F5, F6, Backspace) no longer fire while the editor is open.

Level editor manual: 21 pages, a BUTTONS page per tab made from the UI (every button with its tip), pages for the menus, themes, importing, the mission maker and scenes; the same text ships as EDITOR_MANUAL.txt.

Level editor import: drop an .obj (with its .mtl and pictures) or a png / jpg / tga on the window and it is copied into the library and used; CREATE > OBJ MODELS lists the models with SIZE; png and jpg work as custom textures.

Scenes: stories made of comic panels (picture + caption, voice and music wav), title cards and avi clips (mods/<pack>/scenes/<name>/scene.txt, see tools/MODDING_scenes.txt and mods/_samples/Sample Scene). Played from Extras > Custom Missions, the console (scene <name>), and as the intro / outro scene of a custom mission.
Mission maker: INTRO SCENE / OUTRO SCENE rows; the start, goals, targets and destinations of the draft are drawn as labelled rings in the editor view.

Photo mode and the Customizer take the mouse: Tab shows the pointer in photo mode (click a row to change it, wheel steps, Take Photo button); the Customizer tabs, car / sound lists, paint swatches and wheel cells are clickable. Photo mode: the left stick strafed the wrong way, fixed.

Customizer: the Car and Sound lists have a find box (/ or F3 or Ctrl+F, type a part of a name in any case, Enter keeps the filter, Esc clears it; the first match is chosen when you press Enter). The scroll bars of the lists can be dragged or clicked, and the Lights and Exhaust tabs take mouse clicks (a click chooses an item or row, a second click opens it, a click on the left / right half of a value makes it less / more). 3 new texts, machine translated (native review needed).
Mission maker: NEW / COPY / DELETE buttons for mission slots, and a line under the summary that says what the draft still lacks (no start, no goal, tail without destination ...).
Level editor: in FACES mode a lamp, sign or barrier lights up under the cursor and a click turns it into a piece you can move, turn, scale, copy or delete (before it was only deleted).

Scene composer: the new SCENES tab of the level editor builds scenes with buttons (pictures, captions, voices, music, clips, order, PLAY); drop png / jpg / tga, wav or avi files on the window to add them.

Scenes: slow camera moves over a picture (move=zoomin ... pandown), fades, scenes that continue with another scene (next=), and a mission can continue with another mission (THEN MISSION): a story chain.
Mission maker: STOP, SPEED and POLICE steps for custom missions, a CAR DAMAGE row, slot titles, and browsing the mission slots no longer leaves empty drafts behind.

Setup: the city map pictures are made by the setup now: at the end of the install it lets the game build the map of every city (Driver 2 and the installed Driver 1 cities) with a hidden window (about a minute and a half), and the loading pictures of the Driver 1 cities get their map behind the name. The game no longer has to make them at the first visit of a city.

Yellow Cab: without the Driver 1 disc the cab is the Driver 2 Bel Air repainted yellow with the checker band; the project ships only the painted pixels (an overlay), the rest is made from your own disc.

Driver 1 cities: the Driver 1 cars in the traffic had oversized wheels hanging below the body (the cosmetics file of a mod, BetterCars, for Rio was laid over them). Mods no longer replace the cosmetics, denting and car models of a converted Driver 1 city.

Options > Graphics: Exhaust Pipes (the 3D pipe models), Tail Lamp Glow (the red lens of the tail lamps lighting up) and Handbrake Brake Light (off by default: the handbrake no longer lights the brake lamps; it was one of the reports). View Distance now goes down to 1 (the original game's draw distance).
The flat car shadow (Sun Shadows off) is the static original one again: it no longer stretches away from the sun into a big block; Sun Shadows is the dynamic system.

The car you got out of is not removed by the traffic clean-up any more (the jam breaker and the density trim skip it): it stays at the gas pump while you fill up. Only the normal distance rule removes it, when you are far away.
Driver 1 cities: the Driver 2 cars of Rio (borrowed into the traffic) have their bodies and textures again.

Level editor: a hitch every few frames while the editor was open in a city with many hidden original faces (New York: about 23 000), up to 0.8 s each, is gone. The pick of the original face under the cursor looked every triangle of a 10000 unit box up in the list of hidden faces one by one; they are in a spatial hash now (a pick takes 1 ms instead of 160 - 810 ms).

Traffic cars: the Gran Turismo cars no longer appear in the traffic (they are for the customizer only for now). Developer Options > Traffic Cars: Extended (on = the cars of the level, of the other cities of Driver 1 / Driver 2 and the car packs you switch on; off = vanilla, only the level's own cars) and one row per car pack.

Driver 1 cities: you get out of the car without a crash and Tanner is in every city: the Driver 1 levels have no model of him, so the converter (and the setup, from RIO.LEV of your Driver 2 disc) adds his 16 body parts and his texture page to each city level.
Scenes: seconds=hold keeps a panel until a button is pressed, Left / L1 goes one panel back, a damaged jpg picture no longer closes the game.

Setup (reDriver_Setup.exe): everything the dev game makes from your discs is now made by the setup itself, no Python needed: the Gran Turismo 1 and 2 cars (with pop-up headlights, decals, race cars) and all engine sounds, the Driver 1 / Driver 2 / Gran Turismo 2 wheel designs (Customizer Wheels tab) and the four Driver 1 cities (Take A Ride). New rows for Gran Turismo and Gran Turismo 2 (EBOOT.PBP, .cue/.bin or .iso; the Driver 2 disc 1 is the template of the cars).
Setup also makes the loading pictures of the Driver 1 cities. GT cars: lamps and badges set back under a bigger body panel (taillights of many cars) are drawn in front of it now.

Setup: disc images may stay in a .zip or .7z archive (also both discs, also an archive with several images): the setup unpacks to a temporary folder and cleans it up. .rar and other archive types get a message to unpack them first. All new texts are translated into the 12 setup languages.

Take A Ride lists all eight cities (the four Driver 2 cities and San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami, New York when installed) in the new menu style. The city is always the day level; the time of day is the clock: Day / Dawn / Dusk / Night for the Driver 2 cities, Day / Dawn / Dusk for the Driver 1 cities (Los Angeles is a night city: it always starts at night). Per city data (map, labels, streets, gas stations, jobs, car sounds, level edits) is keyed by a city id, so the Driver 1 cities no longer share Rio's files.

Driver 1 cities: planar water reflections from the water pieces of the edit pack (a flat piece with a texture named water...), a map picture made by the game from the level data for every city (generated on the first start, nothing is shipped), Los Angeles road spikes fixed (instance chains in the converter).

Reflections and the other graphics tweaks apply to the day versions of all four Driver 2 cities; the water reflects the sky and clouds; the button tooltips are translated; the black rectangle around a wheel whose hubcap came off is gone.
Level edits of the pack (the hand made water, canal and bridge pieces for Havana and Rio too) ship in the Core pack.

Police closer to the original game: the backup respawn time is the original (320, it was 170), the cops' speed and strength follow the felony like the original (no Survival strength at the top of the bar), the default Max Chasing Cars is 4. New option Police Options > Patrol Cars (None / Few / Normal / Many, default Few): how many patrol cars the traffic carries (the old value was Normal: with the busy traffic that meant about three cops around you all the time).

Police backup cars never appear in view: they are born out of sight (a cone of 70 degrees ahead up to 240 m and 70 m all round), at least 7 seconds of your speed away (never closer than 100 m), without collisions until they are close and the way is clear, and they wait while the nose is in a wall.

Camera Views: Options > Camera Views (also in the main menu under Controls) chooses which of the 12 views the camera button cycles. Default: 3rd person, bumper, hood. The on-foot view is no longer carried into the next car.
Gamepad: the radio buttons come only from your bindings (Radio / Job: Previous / Next). The shoulder buttons no longer change the station when they are bound to something else.
The siren of your own car (the horn of a car with a siren) now flashes the cop lights on the street.

Driver 1 sounds: the crash sounds of Driver 1 cars are the real crash sounds of the disc (light thud, crunch, heavy crash) instead of the steel barrier and wood fence clangs, and the Driver 1 engine and idle loops play at the pitch of the disc (the per kind tuning is gone). Run the setup again with the Driver 1 disc to get the new sounds.
The shipped config.ini has overrideContent=1 (the content override of mods with car models is on).

Fixed: BetterCars (and any mod with a DRIVER2 folder: car models, .cos cosmetics) did nothing, because config.ini ships overrideContent=0 and that switched the mod content off after the mods had asked for it; the mods now keep it on. Driver 1 cars: the light hit keeps the Driver 2 sound (the Driver 1 sample used for it was the steel barrier clang).

GPU cars: car bodies, undersides, wheel arcs, wheels, damaged cars, cars lit by dynamic lights, car shadows (shadow map), the far ambient traffic and the civilian pedestrians are drawn by the graphics card from static buffers instead of being transformed and lit polygon by polygon on the CPU. Same look (checked frame against frame with tools/ab_cars.py), about 50 % more frames in dense traffic on a fast PC and much more on an old CPU. New option Options > Graphics > GPU Cars and config.ini [game] gpuCars=1 (0 = the original CPU path).

GPU cars: a chrome reflection (streaky sky / horizon sphere map, added over the body and glass) on every car, Driver 2, Driver 1 and Gran Turismo cars; strength follows the Car Reflection option, dims at night. Developer variables REDRIVER_CHROME / REDRIVER_GTREFL set the strength.

Cars: the chrome reflection replaces the old world reflection on the car bodies (one reflection, not two) and also works with the CPU car path. Cars with more than 255 vertices / polygons can be dented now (the dent lists are 16 bit; the old limit also overran the damage level table of models with more than 256 polygons).

Customizer: new Sound tab: pick the engine sound of your car from every sound the game knows (Driver 2 cars, the sound sets of mods' carsounds folders; labels from carsounds/names.txt), heard while you choose. The choice is saved with the car in garage.sav. tools/gtsounds_all.py makes 528 sets from your own Gran Turismo 1 / 2 discs, with every loop of the engine bank: the new layered engine type (Gran Turismo 2 cars play the intake and the exhaust bank together) (carsounds/<set>.layers + <set>_L<k>.wav) crossfades up to 9 loops over the rev range like the Gran Turismo games, the gear shifts of Driver 2 are heard. The audition works while the game is paused.
tools/gt_convert_all.py converts every car of your Gran Turismo 1 and 2 discs into the packs (about 1700 cars); the car catalog holds 2500 entries now.

Lights: L switches the headlights of your car on / off at any time of day, K = high beams (longer, brighter beams), J (held) = the left pop-up headlight goes down (a wink). Pop-up headlights (Gran Turismo 2 Nissan 180SX) move up and down with the lights.

Travel: Pause > Travel changes the city without restarting the game. Driver 1 cities run a day-only clock (sunrise to sunset). Gas stations in Havana, Las Vegas and Rio; street lights in Rio and the Driver 1 cities.
Driver 1 cities: pedestrians walk the pavements (convert the cities again with tools/d1level_to_d2.py).

Driver 1 cities: loading pictures with the city name, no more invisible cars (wheels only), Los Angeles lighting, per city settings in cities\<NAME>.ini / config\city_<0-3>.ini (day only clock, brightness, paints).

Car streaming: the cars of the packs (Driver 1, Gran Turismo 1 / 2 ...) are a catalog; the cars of Driver 1 and the first cars of a pack are loaded at the start, the others when traffic or the Start Car picker needs them and are given up again (least recently used, never a car on the map). Up to 250 car models at a time (was 140), 1200 catalog entries (was 96), 1000 texture rows (was 250), 600000 car polygons (was 56000). Fixed: car texture rows above 127 went negative (garbled cars when many cars were loaded). New in a pack's cars\index.txt: kind=street|race|special (only street cars are traffic) and rarity=<weight> (default 10), pin=1 (always loaded); developer variables REDRIVER_STREAMCARS, REDRIVER_EAGERCARS, REDRIVER_STREAMCOPIES, REDRIVER_STREAMTEST. The cars borrowed from the other Driver 2 cities stream as well; replays name the car of a player (not a slot) and the traffic pick no longer depends on what is loaded, so a replay shows the same cars; the developer showroom loads every streamed car that fits.

Car customizer (pause menu > Customize), three tabs: Car (every installed car in one list: the cars of this city and the other cities, Driver 1, the packs such as Gran Turismo; your car is swapped on the spot, no restart, cars that are not loaded are loaded as you scroll; in Take a Drive), Paint (the paints of that car as swatches) and Wheels (thumbnails of 188 wheel designs: the stock wheels of the four Driver 2 cities and of Driver 1, and the wheel shop of Gran Turismo 2 as a separate set; finishes). The camera shows the car at an angle and turns around it. Wheel files: game\wheels\d2.wheels, d1.wheels (tools\wheelfaces.py, from the discs' levels) and gt2.wheels (tools\gt2wheels.py, from a Gran Turismo 2 disc); the Gran Turismo 1 rims were dropped (too blurry). Texts in 12 languages. New tabs Lights and Exhaust: move the built-in lamps and the exhaust pipe of any car in the 3D view (mouse gizmo or keyboard), add lamps (headlight, taillight, turn signal, running light, side marker, reverse, brake, fog) with a name, colour, size and behavior (always on, brake, gas, reverse, lights on, turn left / right, hazard) and extra exhaust pipes with their own scale and smoke start; the rim size of the wheels is adjustable. Everything is saved per car as text in the Core mod (cars\fx\<car>.carfx). The converted Driver 1 cars and the wheel files are stored in the Core mod now (mods\reDriver 2 Extended Core\cars / wheels). The paint, wheel design and rim size of every car you customize are remembered in your save (saves\<profile>\garage.sav) and put on the car again when you start Take a Drive or pick the car.

Gran Turismo cars: GT1 engine sounds can be extracted (tools\gtsound.py, SOUND.DAT) into the car sound sets; the mapping car -> engine is approximate (by redline), the RX-7 uses it. GT car scale 0.135, ride height, denting without the 255 vertex limit.
All real traffic now uses the full detail car model at any distance (the low detail model is only left for ambient cars); the Car Detail Distance option is gone. The GPU cars make this nearly free.

The modder tools (tools\*.exe) are an optional separate download (reDriver_ModTools_<version>.zip) instead of being in the game package: players do not need them, and the package is a third of its size (34 MB instead of 131 MB) with fewer antivirus false positives. The guides stay in the package.

Setup: the Driver 1 PC cars no longer print a FAILED line for pc_player15 (it is not a car: its model data is a table of normals on every disc); 30 PC cars as before. Nero images use the first data track (audio tracks are skipped); the setup follows the DPI of the monitor it is on.

Logs: the developer trace logs/batchlog.txt (about 130 KB appended on every start, thousands of lines about GPU buffers) and the bridge piece list (logs/bridgelog.txt) are only written when the developer variables REDRIVER_BATCHLOG / REDRIVER_BRIDGELOG are set; shader / framebuffer failures and the bridge summary go into logs/log.txt. A normal run now writes only log.txt, the engine log and a few small files.

CPU use: the game used almost two CPU cores (180 - 190 % of one core, in the main menu too): the 60 Hz "vblank" thread spun without waiting and the frame limiter spun for up to 4 ms of every frame. The thread sleeps until the tick now, the limiter waits on a high resolution timer: about 80 % of one core in play, 30 - 50 % in the menus, same 160 fps. The sound state (music tracker, channel timers) is changed under one lock now, so the vblank thread and the game can no longer change it at the same time (rare sound glitches).

Logic tick cost: the traffic passes look at the cars of the grid cells around a car instead of all 160 slots, the integer square root and the 128 bit division of the traffic maths use a floating point estimate made exact by integer checks (same numbers), and the sound emulation decodes a car sound once instead of at every start (starting a car sound took 1 - 5 ms inside the logic tick). The logic tick of a rush hour with 116 cars: median 0.55 -> 0.42 ms, 99th percentile 2.0 -> 0.8 ms, slowest 6.4 -> 1.2 ms. The traffic behaves exactly as before (the 67 simulation hash scenarios are equal).

Replays: the ping packets of a replay stored the car slot in a signed byte: with up to 160 cars the slots above 127 read as negative numbers (car_data[-n]); fixed. A replay now stores a fingerprint of the simulation settings (traffic, AI, police, physics mode) and of the mods, and the log says when a replay is played with other settings ("it may play differently").
Boats: the cars that ride on a boat were a 32 bit mask: with 160 cars every car above slot 31 stood still while the boat moved and Tanner's bit landed on car 0; a real bit set now.
Level safety: the model tables have 2048 slots (a cell object type is 11 bits), so a damaged or modded level cannot read outside them.

The shipped exe ignores the developer / test environment variables (REDRIVER_*, 326 of them: test beds, traces, cheats of the dev tools); only the Travel restart and the documented options (REDRIVER_D1COP, D1FILES, D1PC, KEEPBARRIERS, RADIODIR, NOFASTCARS, NODEFERPRESENT, NOBATCHCACHE, BATCHLOG) still work. The build is called "Release".
Batch cache: at most 2 files per level (was 4) and 1.5 GB for all levels together; unfinished .tmp files of a crashed write are removed.

Fixed: reading a damaged / modded level could index outside the model and texture tables (barrier scan, roof scan, far renderer); the mission maker's EDIT TEXT crashed on a read only mod folder; running out of memory now writes the size and place into logs\log.txt, shows a message and closes the game instead of crashing.

changelog.title: 0.3.0-beta   2026-10-12   (RELEASED publicly 2026-10-12 - everything since 0.2.0 is listed here; the 0.2.1 - 0.2.8 test builds were never published)

sections.title: Changes
lines: Driver 1 cars: the cars of the PC release have one 16 colour palette for every texture of the car (not one for the whole page) and keep their smooth shading, with six paints (the real palettes of the release); the PlayStation cars keep their original colours. Driver 1 sounds: all Driver 1 cars use the Driver 1 engine and idle loops with three Driver 1 horns, pitched by kind of car (cop, family, luxury, old, muscle, sport, small, truck), the Driver 1 crash sounds (light, medium, heavy) and the Driver 1 tyre skid; the setup builds them from the disc (Driver 1 Sounds mod). Driver 1 police cruisers: half of the police cars (patrols, chase cars and backup) are Driver 1 cruisers with a light bar and the Driver 1 siren (REDRIVER_D1COP=<percent> changes the share).
Driver 1 cities (Pause > Travel) are marked experimental: the ground heights of the converted cities are not right yet (cars can fall off hills where the data jumps); that work is on hold.
Driver 1 cities: the map screen and the minimap have the look of the Chicago map now (red streets, grey land, green parks, pale blue water; finer picture, 256 world units per pixel).

Take a Ride: the barrier slabs that blocked Michigan Ave for no reason are taken out of the level (all the other barriers of the map stay). (REDRIVER_KEEPBARRIERS=1 keeps them.) The tachometer lost the second dark plate behind the digital speed. The new texts (taxi, police, options) are translated in all 12 languages (machine translations, native speaker review welcome).

Taxi: fares pay more at rush hour (dusk, +30 %), at night (+15 %) and in the rain (+25 %); the dispatcher says so in the offer. VIP fares (a singer, a quarterback, the mayor...) pay two and a half times the meter but have rules: no speeding and no bumps, three strikes and they walk, a flawless ride earns a bonus. Night shift: tipsy passengers change their mind about where they are going and may grab the wheel (a patrol car that sees it pulls you over), dodgy passengers may run without paying - stop next to them within ten seconds and they pay.

Police: cops need a clear line of sight now: a building between you and a patrol car hides you (no felony, no pull-over, a chase can be lost behind a corner). Patrol cars are part of the ordinary traffic again, also while you are on a taxi fare or another job (they were never added during a job): police cars driving around or parked at the kerb with the civilian cars (at most two driving ones near you at a time; parked ones do not count) are real patrol cars that watch for offences, pull you over and join a chase.

Controller: the extra buttons of a pad (back paddles / M buttons, e.g. of the 8BitDo Ultimate 2) can be assigned to any action in the controller rebind menu: press the button when the row asks for it ('Extra Button N'). They only work when the pad reports them to Windows (try its D-input / Switch mode if the 2.4G / X-input mode hides them); log.txt has a [pad] line with the number of buttons the pad reports.

Racing wheels (experimental): a steering wheel with pedals works as a controller. Options > Controls > Wheel Controls: Wheel Support (Auto / On / Off), pick the steering, throttle and brake axes by moving them, invert switches, sliders for steering sensitivity / dead zone / curve / smoothing and a dead zone + curve for each pedal, a live view of the input, and Export / Import of the whole wheel setup as a .wheel file (config\wheel profiles) to share. Wheel buttons are bound in Gamepad Controls like any other button. The brake pedal also reverses. The wheel does not press menu buttons. Force feedback (off by default, Wheel Controls > Force Feedback (Experimental)): a centring spring that grows with speed and cornering, a pull when the car slides, a rumble for skids and road noise and a kick in collisions, with sliders for overall strength, centring, road and skid effects, collision jolts, an Invert Force switch and a Test button. It needs a wheel that supports force feedback through DirectInput; it has not been tried on a real wheel.

Gamepad: new option Gamepad Control Mode (Analog Controls / Digital Controls) in the controller settings of the main menu and the pause menu: the pad is held in the chosen mode all the time (the sticks could be dead after a load until Start + Select; Start + Select now flips the option).

Menus reorganized (main menu and pause menu): Graphics is sorted into groups with headings (Quality, Lighting & Shadows, Reflections, World & Sky); the HUD options and the day / night options moved to Display, together with Subtitles; Police Options (Cop Difficulty is its first row) is in the Options list; every option list has group headings (Display, Controls, Sound, Police Options, the keyboard / gamepad / wheel lists and the pause menu's Gameplay list); settings are saved as soon as you change them, no need to quit the game any more.

HUD messages: the popup texts (offences, police, mission messages) are drawn as a plate in the style of the top HUD panels, hanging under the objective / traffic stop panel when there is one, instead of yellow letters over the road view that overlapped it (modern HUD; the classic HUD keeps the old text).

HUD: the money is in a pill (moved clear of the fuel gauge); the d-pad hints under the map show all four directions (Cruise = up, Map = down, Radio = left / right: previous / next station, also the answers of a job offer, with the single left + right icon); the damage and wanted bars are brighter and further from the map, so their icons no longer touch it.

HUD themes: Options > Display > HUD Theme switches between Modern 70s (walnut and orange), PlayStation (navy glass, steel bevels, Driver red and yellow) and Driver Menu (the look of the main menu's option lists: flat translucent black panels, yellow headings, a dark red selection bar, no stripes, and flat gauges and hint pills with a thin red rim). Menu Style (Display) chooses how the pause menu looks independently of the theme: as the theme says, a centred window, or a translucent side panel like the main menu's lists (Driver Menu uses the side panel). Modders can add themes as text files in <mod>\hud\themes\<name>.ini (name, ten colours, accent, corner roundness, bevel, menu, stripes, hud), see mods_README.txt.

HUD: the Driver Menu theme uses muted colours like the original release, more transparent panels, no bar on the hint pills and the red of the original minimap border for the rims and thin lines (map rim, tachometer rim, the line of the side panel menu). The dark disc behind the tachometer is off by default; Options > Display > Gauge Background switches it on.

HUD: the three controls pills under the minimap are a Controls hints panel now: it pops up at the top right when a game starts and again every 10 - 15 minutes for ten seconds (Cruise, Map, Radio with the keys or the d-pad / stick icons); Options > Display > Hints turns it off. The minimap moved down to the height of the speedometer and the whole minimap stack (map, bars, clock) is scaled down to the size of the speedometer stack (the map shows the same part of the city, at a smaller scale).

Pause menu: new Exit To Windows entry (saves, asks first); Mods and Language are in the main pause list; Options has Cheats and Developer Options (was Debug Options) at the end. Developer Options only holds engine and test settings now (time and weather limits, rendering internals, traffic AI tuning, far density, economy and career numbers, debug overlays, skip mission, reset tweaks); everything a player would use is in the normal Options lists only once (no duplicates). The version text is in the title row of the pause menu. The Driver Menu theme is the default for everybody (Options > Display > HUD Theme changes it); the minimap has the same faint shadow as the gauges and is a little lighter.

Credits: Extras > Credits lists the project lead, the contributors (logos, BetterCars, Driver2TextureFixes, the 1977 Caprice), special thanks (the original REDRIVER2 team, the input prompts pack, Reflections Interactive), translators, the libraries used and a short notice; translated into all languages.

Widescreen: the 4:3 pictures of the original menus, the loading screens and the movies are stretched across a widescreen window (Options > Display > Menu Pictures: Stretched / Original 4:3 with black bars); the main menu picture and the game itself are not affected.

Licenses: THIRD_PARTY.txt now carries the Independent JPEG Group acknowledgement, the rxi ini and stb_truetype notices and the right OpenAL Soft license wording, and the package has a licenses folder with the LGPL / zlib / IJG texts.

Fonts: the HUD and the added letters of the game fonts (Greek, Cyrillic, Latin Extended) are made from open fonts now (Jost, Caprasimo, Archivo Black, Anton, Noto Sans; SIL Open Font License) instead of Microsoft fonts; the look is close to the old one (geometric sans, a Cooper Black style soft serif for titles).
Main menu: new ultrawide main menu picture (3440 x 1440).
Pause menu > Options > Credits shows exactly the same credits as the main menu (scrollable).

PHOTO MODE (pause menu > Photo Mode): the game freezes, the HUD is hidden and a free camera starts at the game camera (WASD / mouse or sticks, Q E or triggers for down / up). A small panel sets camera speed, time of day, a colour filter (warm, cool, faded, sepia, night blue), exposure, a vignette with its own strength, size, shape (oval / rounded / square) and colour (black / white / brown), cinematic bars (2.39:1, 2:1, 1.85:1), a thirds grid, a picture frame (white, black, instant photo) and a self timer (3 / 10 s); Reset Effects clears them. Enter / A saves a JPEG of the picture without the panel to the Screenshots folder; H / B hides the panel; Esc / Y goes back to the pause menu.

CUSTOM MISSIONS: Extras > Custom Missions lists the missions that mods bring (MISSIONS\M1000.D2MS to M1199) with title, city and mod, and plays them with the Take A Ride rules (no career progress is touched; the finish menu says Mission Complete / Failed). The level editor (F6) has a MISSION tab to make them without any file work: kind DRIVE (reach a goal), RACE (checkpoints in order against a time limit) or CHASE (wreck a target car that drives off when you come close), time of day, weather, time limit, your car and paint, police, title and messages; START and GOAL + are set at the camera crosshair; SAVE writes the mission into the edit pack, PLAY starts it right away.

MISSION MAKER, more kinds: TAIL (follow a traffic car to its destination without being seen or losing it), ESCAPE (the police come after you, lose them, reach the safe house), DELIVERY (pick up, deliver against the clock, the seconds left are paid as a bonus) and CUSTOM (any steps in any order: go to, wreck, tail, escape, bonus). The finish menu of a custom mission has a Custom Missions list to pick the next one (also in another city). The text format names the texts inside targets too ("name" instead of byte offsets).
Names: the pause menu shows reDriver 2: Extended with the version and the build time; README / setup / tool texts say reDriver 2: Extended everywhere.

ONE CORE PACK: reDriver Core, Chicago Water, Vegas Water, Level Edits and the Driver 1 car sounds are one pack now: reDriver 2: Extended Core (folder mods\reDriver 2 Extended Core). It holds the maps, icons, HUD, car sounds (the Driver 1 engine files are made by the setup from your disc and go into it), the water / canal / bridge fixes and the level edits; the level editor saves into it by default. An older ReDriver Core folder is renamed by the game.

SETUP: more Driver 1 PC releases work: German, Spanish (re-release: its files are in the Joliet tree), French, Italian and English (Nero .nrg image) discs; all give the same 30 cars. Disc images can be .cue / .bin / .iso / .img / .nrg / .pbp.

SETUP: long folder paths (over 260 characters) work (extended-length paths; movies too); long error messages under a disc row are no longer cut off (three-line area); the result list has no line limit.
The release ships The Long Way Home.txt and the mods BetterCars, Chicago Caprice and Driver2TextureFixes.

First start: the graphics settings default to the Max preset (view distance 400, reflections on cars / wet roads / glass / water at 80 / 70 / 60 / 80, dynamic lights) instead of the developer's test values; the main menu picture (mainmenu.png) of the core pack now ships.
LINUX setup (python): reads Nero .nrg images and Joliet-only discs (Spanish Driver 1 PC re-release), like the Windows setup.

SETUP: the drive finder and the "game folder of another build" shortcut are gone from the setup window (a drive scan is the kind of thing SmartScreen / antivirus programs dislike); the disc rows with Browse are all there is. (The command line --import still works.)
LOGO: the new reDriver 2: Extended logo is the icon of the game window / exe, the setup (window, title bar and installer header) and the modder tool exes.

SETUP LANGUAGES: the setup window and its messages are translated into the 12 languages of the game (Windows language, a language box on the first page, --lang xx; the log files stay English). The movie converter (strconv.exe) takes UTF-8 names now, so a game folder with any letters (Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese ...) converts movies too.

SETUP: reDriver_Setup.exe is a native Windows program written in C with a real setup window now (no console, no Python): welcome page, a page for the disc images (one row per disc, every file is checked at once and named in plain words, wrong discs / Driver 1 discs in a Driver 2 row / plain .iso files are explained, a finder that lists the drives of the PC and the disc images on them), the destination folder (free space, earlier installation, nothing outside the game's own files is touched), options with a summary, a progress page (step and overall progress, moving bar when the time cannot be measured, log, Cancel that removes unfinished files), and a result page (what worked, skipped, failed; open the folder, start the game, view the log). The installation runs in the background so the window never freezes. It makes the same files as the Python setup did (disc images, cutscene audio, Driver 1 / PC cars, engine sounds, movies; checked byte for byte except the 16 colour palettes of the PC cars, which are reduced by an own median cut now with the same quality). Command line options are unchanged (+ --dest); setup_log.txt and setup_report.txt are written as before. Linux keeps the Python setup.

LEVEL EDITOR: sprites (FACE CAM turns the selected pieces to the camera; sample objects tree_oak, tree_pine, bush_round, palm_tree in data\objects, made by tools\make_sprite_objects.py), small thumbnails in the object list, scrolling textures (SCROLL U / SCROLL V on the TEXTURE tab, speed = ANIM HZ), RAILS (kerb walls along the sides of selected DRIVE pieces, solid and slanted for ramps).
Menus: Mods (restart to apply) became Mods with a small sublabel; the same for Conflicts (the main menu and the pause menu).

MISSION MAKER: REC CHASE / REC INTRO / REC OUTRO record a chase or the intro / outro cutscene of a custom mission straight from the game you are driving (no tool needed); the script plays the cutscenes by itself.
HUD: the damage and wanted arcs fade out while there is no damage / no felony and fade in when it changes.

MOD MANAGER in the main menu: Options > Mods (switch mods on / off, move them in the load order, an info line per mod with how many files it replaces) and Show Conflicts, a list of the files that two mods both bring; the pause menu's mod list has Show Conflicts too.

CUSTOM MISSIONS: texts follow the language (MISSIONS\M<n>.<Language>.txt of a mod, the game's language files; the mission maker's phrases are translated in all languages; a TRANSLATE button writes the files for translators). New REC CHASE step: a car that drives a route you recorded (Take A Ride + Save replay + chase_tool). Starting a custom mission from the editor or the finish menu reloads the level.
Modder tools: pack_tool (new / check / pack / install / list mods) and chase_tool (recorded chases and cutscenes for missions).

MISSION MAKER, script editing in the game: EDIT TEXT / APPLY / RESET TEXT (every number, the script and the strings of a mission as text in your editor, built again with an error line on a mistake; no Python needed) and the console commands mission dump / build. The panel shows the rows of the steps you use (marker size, target flees, tail range, escape time and wanted level, bonus base pay) and scrolls. A tail has its own distances.
Mods: the console command conflicts and the mod list's info line show which files two switched-on mods both bring.
Modding tools in the package as stand-alone .exe files (mission_tool, iso_tool, lev_dump, loc_report and the two Driver 1 car converters) with tools\MODDING_tools.txt.
Console (the key left of 1): new commands tweak [key [value]], hour, tp x z, missions, mission n, reload (mod tweaks, jobs, taxi talk and the language files are read again without restarting).
Modding: MODDING_GUIDE.txt (start here) and three sample mods in mods\_samples (tweaks, HUD theme, mission).

Modding: mission files (MISSIONS\M<n>.D2MS) can be written as text and built again with tools\mission_tool.py (extract from the disc, dump, build, check); a mod's mission replaces the game's mission of that number. The guide is tools\MODDING_missions.txt.
Fixed: the Y / Triangle button of a gamepad did not resume the game from the first pause menu (only Continue did); the keyboard keeps its old behaviour.

FILM DIRECTOR / replays: the recording tape is about 228 times longer (684,988 instead of 3,000 pad records per player, i.e. hours instead of about 100 seconds; the original code left only 13 KB of the 320 KB replay buffer for it, the buffer is 2 MB now) and a replay can have 250 camera cuts (was 60) and 4096 auto director waypoints (was 150 = about 8 minutes, after which the auto director stopped cutting; its waypoint pointer also could run into the camera table, now bounded). Replays saved with the new version are marked; replays of older versions still load (their camera table is 60 cuts).
Controllers and racing wheels keep working while the game window is not in focus (alt-tab, second monitor, recording software).
Fixed: the front end font had no @ # + = < > ~ ^ | \ ' " (they were blank, e.g. in the credits e-mail address); they are drawn now. The keyboard icon theme defaults to Light.
HUD: the tachometer, the fuel arc and the MPH label have a faint drop shadow, so they stay readable on pale roads and sand now that the dark disc behind them is off.
Fixed: a freeze when the police backup was placed on a junction or off the roads (an endless search for a road piece at a fixed position).

Gamepad: new option Swap D-Pad And Left Stick (Controls): the d-pad steers like the left stick (digital steering) and the left stick presses the d-pad directions (cruise, map, radio, menus); the HUD hints show the stick then.
Fixed: Cop Difficulty and Subtitles were also written to tweaks.ini and could disagree with the profile; they are stored in the profile only now.

Busted: only when the police can see you, two or more cars close in, you stand still AND the car cannot move more than 10 m forward or backward (a vehicle in the lane or a wall): standing still, watching something or hiding is no bust. It ends the game (like drowning or wrecking the car in a pursuit); no fine any more. In Take a Ride the on screen messages (offences, police) are at the top of the screen instead of the middle of the road view.
Police chases: backup cars are called in at the original rhythm (see below for where they appear). The 'Dispatch: backup is on the way' call-out is gone (it gave you too much warning).
Fixed: a crash caused by the street lamp damage counter running one past its table (found from a crash log).
Fixed: the keyboard had no reverse with the Modern controls preset. The down arrow brakes and reverses now (also with the classic preset), like the brake button of the classic layout.

Hide HUD option (Options > Graphics, and the pause menu Graphics / Debug lists): turns off the gauges, map, radio panel and mission overlays for screenshots and videos. The pause menu can now be opened in the free camera too (not while the level editor is active).

Water reflections in every city: a flat edit piece with a custom texture whose file name starts with 'water' (like Chicago Water's water_blue.tga) now gets the planar reflections of the city, at the height of that piece. Level editor: a new piece without a picked texture takes the texture of the surface under the cursor instead of showing noise.

Saved games are plain text files in the game's saves\default folder (profile.sav: settings, furthest mission, secrets, high scores; progress.sav: the continue point; money.ini, respect.ini, fare_serial.ini: the career) instead of binary files hidden in your user folder. Copy or zip the folder to back it up or share it; REDRIVER_PROFILE=<name> keeps another player's saves in saves\<name>. Every file has a format number, unknown entries are ignored and written back, missing ones get defaults, and the previous version of each file is kept as .bak, so an update will not break your saves. Old saves are picked up automatically.

Level editor: barriers, street lamps, signs and other whole objects can be deleted now (click the object to take it over: it is deleted as a whole and stays deleted, also when the area streams in again). They used to be impossible to delete because the game draws them one by one and not from the batches the editor hides faces in. Taxi: any cab that spawns in traffic (Driver 1 cabs too) can be used for fares, and the drop-off marker shows the street name.

Serial stories: passengers now sometimes tell a long story (about two to three minutes a part, with several choices) that lasts the whole fare. Five serials with three parts each (a bakery that is not just a bakery, the treasure of Uncle Mort, the night clerk of a haunted hotel, a wife with a secret life, the caller on the night radio). If the fare ends in the middle, or the part ends, the dispatcher can call you again with the same passenger, who picks up where he stopped ("Now, where was I?"); the progress is saved (saves\default\fare_serial.ini). Only crashes cost mood now (red lights and the wrong side of the road do not), and an average above 60 mph for fifteen seconds without a crash is the fast bonus.

Taxi passengers are much more forgiving: speed, hard braking and police chases no longer upset them (this is a wheelman game); only crashes cost mood and a passenger only walks out after a lot of those. Smooth driving and fast, clean driving earn a bonus on the tip (up to +40 %). Passengers start talking 8-16 seconds into the ride (they hardly ever told a story before) and the talk panel of a passenger has a plain green light instead of the police lights.

Fixed: answering a prompt with the d-pad (CB offers, the taxi dispatcher, briefings, the officer, the passenger's questions) also changed the radio station. The d-pad does not touch the radio while a prompt is open or for a moment after it closes.

Pedestrians can be run over: they no longer always run clear of your car (some are distracted, most are alert but a fast car leaves little time; honking and slow driving still make everybody dodge), and when the body of your car hits one he is thrown, tumbles, bounces and slides along the road, then lies there with limp limbs for about 20 seconds. Hitting a pedestrian is an offence (hit and run). Switch: Gameplay > Run Over Pedestrians (also in the front end Police list). Traffic cars never hit pedestrians.

Gamepad controls have a Preset row at the top (main menu Options > Controls > Gamepad Controls and the pause menu): Modern Controls (triggers for gas and brake, separate reverse, d-pad functions) or Classic Controls (the original PlayStation layout: X gas, square brake / reverse, circle wheelspin, triangle handbrake, the shoulders and triggers as before). Rebinding a button after that shows the preset as Custom.
Fixed: a burnout (the wheelspin button) no longer stalls at about 50 mph; the hand-over to normal acceleration used to be treated as a light touch of the analog trigger (20 % power).

More talk variety (GTA-style satire, PG-13): about 1,170 passenger stories and small talks now (revenge of the pigeons, the man who sold a 'genuine antique', a sandwich-shop heist, the mime in the box ...) and four new CB themes (the absurd, fake commercials, crackpots, neighbours). CB chatter comes about every 45 seconds, job offers 1-2 minutes after a pass or timeout and 3 minutes after you accept one (taxi dispatcher calls are unchanged).

People and talk: everybody you talk to in person has a name now (fares, the traffic stop officer: 'Officer Kowalski', ~330 male, ~220 female first names and ~790 surnames); the dispatcher tells you the fare's name. Passengers no longer comment on every bump: their mood about your driving only moves the tip and they remark on it now and then; they talk to you instead. About 780 stories and small talks with answers: left = aggressive (rude, funny), right = polite, nothing = a neutral line; the story forks on what you say, every story has random names, places, food ... filled in, and the last 330 stories are not repeated. The CB radio is ordinary 70s civilian chatter (not truckers): 360 situations in ten themes (traffic, weather, food, family, work, fun, gossip, radio talk, shopping, car trouble), each with comments, closing lines and openers that combine into thousands of different messages, thousands of callsigns like 'Lucky Pike' or 'Stockyard Sam', and no repeats of the last 90 situations.

Taxi, part 2: pedestrians on the kerb wave down the empty cab (stop within 25 s, setting Taxi Hailing); TOUR fares (about one in five in Chicago): the tourist names a district, you drive around in it for about a minute, he names the next, three districts, then back to his hotel, with a tour bonus on the fare; the roof sign of the yellow cab is lit while it is free (and the cabs in traffic light up now and then).

Taxi: a dispatcher now calls the fares on the CB radio (street name, distance, direction, length of the ride and the estimated fare; Y takes it, N passes, 15-30 s to the next call); turn it off in Pause > Gameplay > Taxi Dispatcher to get the old self-starting fares. Passengers watch your driving: bumps, hard braking, speeding, red lights, the wrong side of the road and the police on your tail get remarks, their mood drops and so does the tip; a passenger who has had enough gets out without paying. A long smooth stretch is praised.

Police (Take a Ride), part 2: backup is called during a chase (extra cars appear far out of sight as ghosts, race to you and turn solid once they are close and nothing is in the way; spawn rate about 10 % faster than the original); the police get faster, stronger and ram you more the higher the felony (the top of the bar feels like Survival); boxed in by the police at a standstill = BUSTED (fine, the chase ends). Offences within three seconds count once (the worst one) and a stop adds them all to one ticket; the felony bar shows the worst of them and is cleared after the stop. Offence Severity list: how much each offence adds to the felony.

Traffic stops: you have 10 seconds to reach the stop point (60-100 m ahead); blowing past it, driving off or ignoring it starts a chase at half the felony bar. The officer walks to your door, faces it and talks to you: he asks if you know why he stopped you and lists the real reasons, with a popup where left = aggressive, right = polite and doing nothing = neutral (Y / N keys or the d-pad). Every answer is a real line: the neutral one is said when you press nothing and just keeps the conversation going, polite sways the officer towards a warning or a dropped offence, aggressive is for fun (name calling, snappy comebacks) and costs you leniency, and real abuse (calling him a pig) turns the stop into a chase. Many more lines of dialog. When the stop is over the officer walks back to his car, gets in and the normal traffic AI takes the car again (new route from where it stands, lane change around you when there is a lane free).
